metadata.topic: Nutrition — Saprophytic, Heterotrophic, and Autotrophic Nutrition
metadata.note: Match 3 nutrition terms to their definitions. 3 slots × 1m each. Word bank: 5 definitions (3 correct + 2 distractors). Autotrophic = self-feeding via photosynthesis; Heterotrophic = feeding on other organisms; Saprophytic = feeding on dead/decaying matter via extracellular digestion.

question.name: CSEC Bio May 2022 Q2a — Define Saprophytic, Heterotrophic, Autotrophic Nutrition
question.text:
Match each type of nutrition to its correct definition by dragging the appropriate phrase into each blank:

Type of NutritionDefinition
Saprophytic[[1]]
Heterotrophic[[2]]
Autotrophic[[3]]
question.general_feedback:
Types of nutrition:

  • Saprophytic: Obtains nutrition by secreting enzymes onto dead/decaying organic matter and absorbing the digested products (e.g. fungi, some bacteria)
  • Heterotrophic: Cannot manufacture own food; obtains organic nutrients by consuming other organisms or organic matter (e.g. animals, most fungi, most bacteria)
  • Autotrophic: Manufactures own food from simple inorganic molecules (CO₂ and water) using light energy (e.g. green plants, algae, cyanobacteria)

Note: Saprophytic nutrition is a sub-type of heterotrophic nutrition — saprophytes are heterotrophs that feed specifically on dead matter via external digestion.

groups.label: Define Saprophytic nutrition
groups.diagnostic_hint: Saprophytic organisms (fungi, some bacteria) secrete digestive enzymes onto dead matter and absorb the products — this is external digestion. Example: mushrooms decomposing a log.

Manufactures own food from simple inorganic substances using light energy
Obtains energy by breaking down inorganic compounds (chemosynthesis)
Feeds by engulfing and internally digesting other whole organisms

groups.label: Define Heterotrophic nutrition
groups.diagnostic_hint: Heterotrophs cannot make their own food — they must consume organic matter from other organisms. This includes animals, fungi, and most bacteria.

options.text: Feeds on dead or decaying organic matter using external digestion

groups.label: Define Autotrophic nutrition
groups.diagnostic_hint: Autotrophs manufacture their own food from inorganic substances using an energy source. Green plants use light energy (photosynthesis); some bacteria use chemical energy (chemosynthesis).

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 5 tokens for 3 slots; 3 correct + 2 distractors. 'Obtains energy by breaking down inorganic compounds (chemosynthesis)' — this describes chemoautotrophy (bacteria like Nitrosomonas), a plausible distractor for autotrophic since it involves inorganic inputs but uses chemical not light energy. 'Feeds by engulfing and internally digesting other whole organisms' — this describes holozoic/phagotrophic heterotrophic nutrition (like Amoeba), a distractor that catches students who confuse holozoic with saprophytic (both are heterotrophic, but the mechanism differs).
